teams.heading: Former winger Chris Ashton admits he is 'still p*ssed off' about England
teams.body: Former England winger Chris Ashton has admitted he remains deeply unsatisfied with his international career, stating he is "still p*ssed off" about how his time in the national shirt unfolded. Despite scoring 20 tries in 44 Test appearances and winning two Six Nations titles, the Premiership's all-time record try scorer revealed he wanted "way more" from his time with England. Now working as a television pundit, the 39-year-old confessed that his perceived failure to truly establish himself on the international stage still bothers him.

teams.heading: Darcy Graham Ruled Out Of Scotland Tests Following Severe Bicep Injury
teams.body: Scotland and Edinburgh winger Darcy Graham faces a minimum of 12 weeks on the sidelines after rupturing his bicep during a recent friendly. The 29-year-old, who has scored 38 tries in 57 Tests, will miss the upcoming autumn series at Murrayfield. Edinburgh head coach Sean Everitt confirmed the news during his team announcement on Friday, noting the injury was a "pretty freakish" collision. The recovery timeline rules the talismanic flyer out of Scotland's November fixtures against New Zealand, Australia, and Japan.

teams.heading: Wales women seek back-to-back victories in challenging USA Test fixture

Head coach Sean Lynn has confirmed that Lleucu George will return to start at fly-half following the injury to Seren Lockwood, who is observing return-to-play protocols. With Carys Cox also returning to the wing, Lynn noted, "I'm super excited to see the half-back combination that we've got this week." Wales are targeting their first consecutive Test wins under his tenure.

teams.heading: Les Kiss shifts Joseph Suaalii to wing for Springboks Test match
teams.body: Les Kiss has gambled on a significant positional change for Sunday’s showdown with the world champion Springboks, naming Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii on the wing for the first time in his 25-Test career. While Suaalii has previously been deployed exclusively in the centres, the head coach is banking on his aerial prowess to counter South Africa’s kicking game. Australia will also employ a 6-2 forward-heavy bench split, with Kiss stating, “we have worked hard on key areas to meet this challenge.”
